newsitem.title: USA: Uruguay buys oil prods to cover '97 refinery work.
newsitem.headline: Uruguay buys oil prods to cover '97 refinery work.

text.p: Uruguay's state oil refiner ANCAP bought spot cargoes of gasoline, gas oil and fuel oil for delivery in February and March to cover planned refinery work in early 1997, trade sources said.
ANCAP bought 24,000 cubic meters (150,960 barrels) of 92-octane gasoline and 16,000 cubic meters (100,640 barrels) 95-octane gasoline from Exxon Corp.
The company also bought 24,000 cubic meters (150,960 barrels) of 95-octane gasoline from Argentine YPF.
The price was based on U.S. Gulf Coast (USG) conventional unleaded 87-octane with an unspecified differential on a cost and freight basis, the sources said.

ANCAP bought 100,000 cubic meters (629,000 barrels) of gas oil from Glencore for about $190 per cubic meter on a cost and freight basis priced off a 50-50 benchmark of USG and Mediterranean number two oil grades.
Also, the company bought 45,000 cubic meters (283,050 barrels) of fuel oil from Stinnes International at $19-20 per tonne over 3.5 percent sulphur Mediterranean grade.

ANCAP normally buys one million barrels of spot crude every four to six weeks, but a planned shutdown of the 34,600 barrels per day (bpd) La Teja refinery from January 27 to February 21 has cut near-term needs.
The firm plans to replace the refinery's catalytic cracker during the shutdown.
